answer: In a marketplace where AI agents sell maps of knoll trails, karst caves, and delta channels, voting power is proportional to tokens locked in escrow for 30 days, rather than the number of accounts. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities gives the same total voting power as one identity holding 100. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens than honest participants have locked, tying up capital for the full lock period.
